About the Biomedical Debate event

Biomedical Debate is a Teamwork event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · speech & presentation.

Ten in-depth lessons for the HOSA Biomedical Debate team event and its 2026–27 resolution: “Limited healthcare resources should be allocated to patients with the greatest likelihood of long-term survival.” Covers scarcity and micro, meso and macro allocation, ethical theories of rationing, allocation criteria and frameworks, real cases from organ transplantation to COVID-19 triage, full affirmative and negative cases using the official references (Levy’s Breaking the Age Code, Bognar and Hirose, the Lancet framework and GESDA longevity science), the six-speech debate format, refutation and weighing, delivery and decorum and preparation for the qualifying test. Includes theory sorting, refutation sequencing, evidence-reading labs and debate scenarios.

Sample Biomedical Debate questions

1. The “rule of rescue” describes the tendency to:

  1. Treat only patients who can pay
  2. Spend heavily to save identified people
  3. Rescue the oldest patients first
  4. Ignore people in immediate danger
Show answer

B. Spend heavily to save identified people

People feel strongly obligated to save identifiable lives in danger, even when cost-effectiveness would favor other uses.

2. Why must an affirmative team define “long-term survival” as individualized and evidence-based?

  1. To exclude all patients over 50
  2. To avoid using age or disability as stand-ins
  3. To rely only on a doctor’s intuition
  4. To keep the criteria hidden from the public
Show answer

B. To avoid using age or disability as stand-ins

Blanket categories invite discrimination claims; patient-specific clinical evidence is more defensible.

3. A physician chooses which of two patients receives the last ICU bed. What level of allocation is this?

  1. Meso
  2. Macro
  3. Systemic
  4. Micro
Show answer

D. Micro

Bedside choices between identifiable patients are micro-level decisions, the hardest to make without a policy.
